newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. army widens probe into scandal at German base.
newsitem.headline: U.S. army widens probe into scandal at German base.

text.p: The U.S. army said on Monday it has widened its probe of three male instructors at a base in Germany after investigators identified 10 other possible victims of sexual misconduct and harassment.

Investigators have so far identified 21 female soldiers who are "potential victims" of mistreatment by the instructors at a training centre in Darmstadt, near Frankfurt, the U.S. Army European Command in Heidelberg said in a statement.

No charges have been filed against the three men, including the two who were being held in custody, as prosecutors were still investigating whether there are more suspects or victims than those already identified.
"To my understanding, we are still dealing with these three alleged perpetrators," an army spokesman told Reuters.
The Darmstadt scandal is one of several sexual harassment scandals to have surfaced in the army since November and the first in the army's European command.
The three instructors, who held the rank of sergeant, are under investigation for alleged offences ranging from rape and forcible sodomy to sexual harassment.

The incidents allegedly took place at the training centre, where new soldiers arriving for duty in the Darmstadt area spend two weeks in an orientation programme, from November to January, according to army officials.
The army last week replaced the male commander of the Darmstadt training centre with a woman.
